items.text: Revenue by customer, concentration of the largest customers, retention and expansion over the last two years, and the typical sales cycle.
items.why: At this stage the investment case rests on revenue quality, which public sources do not show.

items.text: Revenue quality: what drives growth, how retention and expansion differ by customer cohort, and the payback on sales and marketing spend.
items.why: Recurring-revenue quality is the core of a subscription business.

items.text: How the company charges: pricing basis, typical contract size and term, and who pays.
items.why: No pricing is public; price and contract terms set the revenue model.

items.text: Revenue for the last financial year and the year to date, gross margin, operating costs, burn and runway.
items.why: Reported revenue needs the financial statements behind it.

items.text: Which segment and geography the company is prioritising - among mid-sized businesses, D2C and manufacturing companies, fintech and SaaS companies and other segments - why that one first, and how many qualifying sites or customers it counts there.
items.why: Research lists several target segments; the first one sets the sales cycle, reference customers and capital need.

items.text: The buying process in the target segment: budget owner, decision-makers, procurement steps and time from first contact to order.
items.why: Enterprise purchases involve several functions; the observed cycle sets how fast orders can follow.

items.text: Lead and major investors in each financing and the instruments used.
items.why: No lead investor is named in the record.

items.text: Current fundraising: amount sought, capital already committed, use of funds, and the technical and commercial milestones it is meant to reach.
items.why: Links the investment to specific milestones.

items.text: Operating performance of the current offering over the last 12 months: reliability, uptime or service levels, and material incidents.
items.why: Shows whether the offering performs consistently at scale.

items.text: Certification or qualification required for customer operation, its current status and what remains.
items.why: Determines when the product can be sold and used.

items.text: What is protected: patents or applications filed, and ownership of the core technology.
items.why: No patent position is established; defensibility depends on what the company owns and can protect.

items.text: Alternatives actually weighed in customer discussions to date (for example continuing with manual finance operations using spreadsheets and email, or direct alternatives such as ERPNext), why the customer chose or would choose the company, what would stop a competitor replicating the offering, and any comparative cost or performance evidence.
items.why: Only buyer decisions show which alternatives compete; public research shows the field, not the customer's shortlist.

items.text: Current headcount by function and the key hires planned, including who leads enterprise sales.
items.why: Senior roles are held by the founders; the next stage needs sales and delivery capacity.

items.text: Ownership of the company: founders' shareholdings, option pool, founder vesting, and rights attached to the 2025-2026 financings.
items.why: Determines founder incentives and the rights a new investor would rank alongside.

items.text: The legal entity behind the company - registered name, jurisdiction and registration number - and that it is active.
items.why: Financing, contracts and intellectual property attach to a specific legal entity.

items.text: Licences or regulatory permissions held or required, and the compliance and AML / KYC arrangements.
items.why: Regulated activity cannot scale without them.

blocks: Mysa provides AI-powered accounts payable and finance automation. Its offering includes Accounts Payable, Integrated Banking, AI Accounting and Expense Management. It targets mid-sized businesses, D2C and manufacturing companies and fintech and SaaS companies, among other segments, with India as the named market. The revenue model is subscription, sold to enterprise customers through enterprise selling.

It has completed two financings between 2025 and 2026. A financing event, undated was also reported; its completion has not been confirmed.
